summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (LuF 2/35)

data.turoyo: Haṯe i barṯo di ḥurma maraḥtaṯe, d hawxa əbʕowa mbahdlo i sowuṯayḏi l qəl ʕayni.
data.translation: Ist sie doch die Tochter dieser schamlosen Frau, die so mein Alter in Schande bringen wollte, vor meinen Augen...

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: old age stands for the affected older man; abstract participant extension.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Besim Martyrdom of Maferyono/10)

data.turoyo: Lu+ăġano mǝḷḷe, ‘Hano kəmḥaram u+muklayḏan, ŭ komoḥe bi+ṭayuṯo, kul+mede di+ṭayuṯo kəmbahdela. Yani, lǝ+komaqbal mede mdi+ṭayuṯo’.
data.translation: This agha said, ‘This one prohibits our food and he strikes at Islam, he dishonours everything about Islam. That is, he doesn’t accept anything from Islam’.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: abstract religious patient, with object resumption to be checked.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (76/113)

data.turoyo: W ono kobaʕno mbahdanno ruḥi bi qriṯo?
data.translation: Und soll ich mich etwa im Dorfe bloßstellen?

rationale: Completes ordinary Infectum cell to five: overt reflexive ruḥi with active morphology, contrasting with Detransitive.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (107/122)

data.turoyo: elo d marmšat ruḥux, ḥur, gqəṭlolux w gəmbahdlat ono stene ʕam ruḥux.
data.translation: Wenn du dich bewegst, gib acht, dann wird sie dich töten, und du wirst mich und dich zugleich in Schande bringen.

rationale: Unusual independent object pronoun ono with second-person actor and ʕam ruḥux; adds argument-coding evidence beyond ordinary filling.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (95/38)

data.turoyo: Mbahdelux əšme d babe d ruḥux, mbahdelux ʕam ruḥux!
data.translation: du bringst den Namen deines Vaters samt deinem eigenen in Schande

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: 2sg agent, father's name as metonymic patient, and repeated ʕam-phrase.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (113/194)

data.turoyo: Mən yo ma mbahdeluxlan bu ḥaləq ruḥax ʕal i arʕo?
data.translation: Was ist denn? du hast mich ja in Schande gebracht mit deinem "Wirf dich auf die Erde!"

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: 2sg agent plus 1pl patient -lan; edition's singular translation retained and questioned.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (56/95)

data.turoyo: gzayʕo, d lo mahzəm w gmibahdəl.
data.translation: Sie fürchtete nämlich, daß er es mit der Angst kriegen und davonlaufen und so in Schimpf und Schande kommen würde.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell: anticipated disgrace caused by fleeing, without an expressed humiliator.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (93/64)

data.turoyo: w a=tloṯo abne ste w i=aṯto ste mayiṯi w fayəš hiye b tane, hawxa mbahdəl w mayəṯ m u=kafno.
data.translation: und auch die drei Söhre und die Frau starben, und er blieb ganz allein in Schimpf und Schande und starb den Hungertod.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Preterit cell: resulting destitution clarifies the inherited miserable-state example.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
before: in Schimpf und Schande kommen, beschämt dastehen;
after: in Schimpf und Schande kommen, beschämt dastehen; in einen erbärmlichen Zustand geraten;
rationale: The inherited 73/164 already describes torn clothes and misery, and 93/64 describes bereavement and destitution without a public shamer; make that existing broader result state explicit.

summary: The inherited glossary files the Arabic quadriliteral as stem I; do not create Q from a generic quadriliteral analysis.
Active ruḥi constructions deliberately represent self-disgracing action, contrasting with Detransitive disgrace or misery without an expressed external agent.
Detransitive Preterit includes resultant miserable condition, already visible at 73/164; 93/64 broadens its evidence from torn clothes to bereavement and starvation.
Actor and patient endings are distinct: mbahdeluxlan indexes a second-person actor and first-person plural affected group, whereas Infectum can use an independent pronoun (ono) or a suffix.
MAC kəmbahdela has an abstract religious topic; feminine object resumption may track ṭayuṯo rather than masculine mede. No religious technical sense follows from that participant choice.
Repeated free combinations with ruḥo or abstract objects do not establish an additional fixed idiom; all are kept within existing senses.
Does final -a in MAC Besim /10 resume feminine ṭayuṯo through kul mede, or have another analysis?
In 95/38 does ʕam ruḥux mean yourself too, or accompaniment with the preceding name object?
At 113/194 does plural -lan refer to the speaker's group or a pragmatic self-reference? The German has mich; the edition wording is retained.
Confirm the segmental contraction in 1sg mbahdanno and the scope of the result-state Detransitive in 93/64.
Old age, a father's name and religion can stand as abstract patients of disgrace; these participant changes retain the same shaming meaning.
